text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Social Ministry and the emergency medical aid council have agreed to amend the financing of emergency services. The services will be financed from the ministry budget instead of local funds.
- The Coalition Party rejected the rural parties' calls for customs tariffs and subsidies for agriculture.

- The traffic commission intends to limit the speed of heavy vehicles on country roads following the tragic accident in Pala, where a runaway truck killed eight pupils in a collision with a school bus.
- The Union Bank wants to buy the North-Estonian Bank. Negotiations are to begin in November and the merger can take place in the first half of 1997.
